primary_threads: Kingdom and kingship; The people of God; The day of the Lord; Sacrifice and atonement
pre_where: The seventh trumpet has announced that the world's kingdom belongs to the Lord and his Messiah. Today John sees a woman, a child and a dragon (12:1–4).
pre_watch: Watch for how they triumph in 12:11, the Lamb on Mount Zion in 14:1–5, and the call in 14:12.
q1: A woman and her child appear in a vision and the dragon wages war; beasts demand worship, while the Lamb stands with his people on Mount Zion and angels announce judgment. "This calls for patient endurance on the part of the people of God who keep his commands and remain faithful to Jesus" (14:12). What does this reveal about the practice of perseverance?
q2: John calls the dragon "that ancient serpent called the devil, or Satan" (12:9), recalling the serpent of Genesis 3 (Day 1). How does Revelation draw on the Genesis account? Revelation 12:17 speaks of "those who keep God's commands and hold fast their testimony about Jesus"; what does this reveal about God's people as those who hold fast their testimony about Jesus?
q3: In light of the call for patient endurance among God's people, how might perseverance take shape in your life this week?
identity: Those who hold fast their testimony about Jesus

main_theme: Those victorious over the beast sing the song of Moses and of the Lamb, and seven bowls of God's wrath are poured out on the earth.
primary_threads: The day of the Lord; Exodus and redemption; Temple and God's presence
pre_where: Angels have announced the hour of judgment. Today John sees those victorious over the beast standing beside a sea of glass (15:2).
pre_watch: Watch for the song in 15:3–4, the temple filled with smoke in 15:8, and the call in 16:15.
q1: Those victorious over the beast sing the song of Moses and of the Lamb, and seven bowls of God's wrath are poured out on the earth. Jesus says, "Look, I come like a thief! Blessed is the one who stays awake" (16:15). What does this reveal about the practice of watchfulness?
q2: Those victorious over the beast sing "the song of God's servant Moses and of the Lamb" (15:2–4), recalling the song at the sea in Exodus 15:1–18 (Day 21). How does Revelation draw on Moses' song? What does this reveal about God's people as those who remain faithful to Jesus (14:12)?
q3: In light of Jesus' words, "Blessed is the one who stays awake," how might watchfulness take shape in your life this week?
identity: Those who remain faithful to Jesus

main_theme: Babylon the great, pictured as a prostitute riding a beast, falls, and kings, merchants and sailors mourn her destruction.
primary_threads: Kingdom and kingship; Blessing and curse
pre_where: Seven bowls of wrath have been poured out. Today an angel shows John Babylon the great (17:1–5).
pre_watch: Watch for who is with the Lamb in 17:14, the call in 18:4, and the mourning in 18:9–19.
q1: Babylon the great, pictured as a prostitute riding a beast, falls, and kings, merchants and sailors mourn her destruction. A voice from heaven says, "Come out of her, my people," so that you will not share in her sins (18:4). What does this reveal about the practice of holiness?
q2: The voice calls God's people to come out of Babylon so that they will not share in her sins (18:4). First John 2:15–17 (Day 346) says, "Do not love the world or anything in the world… The world and its desires pass away, but whoever does the will of God lives forever." How are these two passages similar or different? What does this reveal about God's people as those who do the will of God and live forever?
q3: In light of the call not to share in Babylon's sins, how might holiness take shape in your life this week?
identity: Those who do the will of God and live forever

main_theme: Heaven celebrates the wedding supper of the Lamb, a rider called Faithful and True defeats the beast, Satan is bound for a thousand years, and the dead are judged.
primary_threads: Kingdom and kingship; The day of the Lord; The people of God
pre_where: Babylon has fallen. Today John hears a great multitude in heaven shouting, "Hallelujah!" (19:1).
pre_watch: Watch for the wedding of the Lamb in 19:6–9, the rider's names in 19:11–16, and the books opened in 20:12.
q1: Heaven celebrates the wedding supper of the Lamb, a rider called Faithful and True defeats the beast, Satan is bound for a thousand years, and the dead are judged. The multitude says, "Let us rejoice and be glad and give him glory! For the wedding of the Lamb has come, and his bride has made herself ready" (19:7). What does this reveal about the practice of joy?
q2: Jesus tells of a king inviting guests to his son's wedding banquet, including the warning in Matthew 22:11–14 (Day 246). How is this picture similar to or different from the blessing pronounced on those invited to the Lamb's wedding supper (Revelation 19:9)? What does the blessing reveal about those invited?
q3: In light of heaven's rejoicing at the wedding of the Lamb, how might joy take shape in your life this week?
identity: Those invited to the wedding supper of the Lamb

main_theme: John sees a new heaven and a new earth and the new Jerusalem, where God dwells with his people and the river of life flows, and Jesus says he is coming soon.
primary_threads: Creation and new creation; Temple and God's presence; The people of God; Kingdom and kingship; Covenant; Blessing and curse
pre_where: John has seen the dead judged. Today he sees "a new heaven and a new earth" (21:1), and the story that began in Genesis comes to its close.
pre_watch: Watch for the voice from the throne in 21:3–5, the river and tree of life in 22:1–3, and the invitation in 22:17.
q1: John sees a new heaven and a new earth and the new Jerusalem, where God dwells with his people and the river of life flows, and Jesus says he is coming soon. The Spirit and bride say "Come," the hearer is invited to say "Come," and the thirsty are invited to take the water of life freely (22:17). What does this reveal about the practice of witness?
q2: John sees the tree of life and hears that "No longer will there be any curse" (22:2–3), recalling the tree of life and the curse in Genesis 2–3 (Day 1). How does the story's end recall its beginning? Revelation 21:3 says, "They will be his people, and God himself will be with them and be their God"; what does this reveal about God's people as those with whom God dwells?
q3: In light of the invitation to the thirsty to receive the water of life freely (22:17), how might witness take shape in your life this week?
identity: Those with whom God dwells
